note: Key sizes 1024, 2048 (default) and 4096, public exponent 65537, output PEM (the public key as PUBLIC KEY, then the private key as RSA PRIVATE KEY, the order and formats of CyberChef), JWK (public key, private key, one line of JSON each; CyberChef's JSON output is a node-forge BigInteger dump, so a real JWK is offered instead) or DER (the private key as PKCS#1 bytes, as CyberChef). The primes come from random:bytes-of only (the op carries +random) through a private prime-search primitive: trial division by the primes below 65536, then 13 Miller-Rabin rounds (base 2 and 12 random bases); a 4096-bit pair takes 1.8 s on average (slowest of twelve runs 3.4 s). Differences: PEM has line feeds where CyberChef (node-forge) writes CRLF (hidden carriage returns in a text pane help nobody, and every PEM reader takes both). The key text can be pasted whole into the other RSA ops. Cross-checked in the wave 7 close-out against CyberChef 11.5.0 (module source read; the module was run on sample inputs for layouts). Kept different: default size 2048 (CyberChef's first option, 1024, is weak).

Cross-checked in the wave 7 close-out against CyberChef 11.5.0 (module source read; the module was run on sample inputs for layouts). Signs the input with a PEM private key (RSA PRIVATE KEY, PRIVATE KEY, ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY or an old-style encrypted PEM; the password parameter is CyberChef's Key Password) and a digest from CyberChef's list (SHA-1 by default, MD5, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512), RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, as raw bytes. Addition: a scheme parameter with RSASSA-PSS (random salt, salt-length parameter) which CyberChef does not offer; the default is unchanged. Encrypted keys: AES-128/192/256-CBC, Triple DES and DES, in the legacy DEK-Info form and in PKCS#8 PBES2 with PBKDF2 (SHA-1, -256, -384, -512); other schemes are E_RANGE. A key that is not RSA is E_RANGE and a damaged key E_COERCE. Parameter order and message-format options were compared with the module source (RSA Verify message formats are Raw, Hex, Base64; Forge adds Latin-1 and reads Raw as UTF-8, and the result texts Verified OK and Verification Failure are CyberChef's).

Cross-checked in the wave 7 close-out against CyberChef 11.5.0 (module source read; the module was run on sample inputs for layouts). The input is the signature; the message is a parameter (UTF-8 text by default, hex, Latin-1 or Base64 for bytes), with the public key (PUBLIC KEY or RSA PUBLIC KEY) and the digest. The result is the text Verified OK or Verification Failure; any fault in the signature is a failed verification, not an error. RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 as in CyberChef, and RSASSA-PSS behind the scheme parameter (salt-length -1 accepts any salt size). Parameter order and message-format options were compared with the module source (RSA Verify message formats are Raw, Hex, Base64; Forge adds Latin-1 and reads Raw as UTF-8, and the result texts Verified OK and Verification Failure are CyberChef's).

Cross-checked in the wave 7 close-out against CyberChef 11.5.0 (module source read; the module was run on sample inputs for layouts). Encrypts the input with a PEM public key under RSA-OAEP (default; the digest is the label hash and the MGF1 hash, with an empty label, as in OpenSSL and node-forge), RSAES-PKCS1-V1_5 or RAW (textbook RSA, no padding), digests SHA-1 (default), MD5, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512. A message that is too long, or for RAW not below the modulus, is E_RANGE. The output has the length of the modulus; OAEP and v1.5 use random bytes (+random). Parameter order and message-format options were compared with the module source (RSA Verify message formats are Raw, Hex, Base64; Forge adds Latin-1 and reads Raw as UTF-8, and the result texts Verified OK and Verification Failure are CyberChef's).

Cross-checked in the wave 7 close-out against CyberChef 11.5.0 (module source read; the module was run on sample inputs for layouts). Decrypts with a PEM private key (as RSA Sign, with the Key Password), RSA-OAEP, RSAES-PKCS1-V1_5 or RAW and the digest. Every failure of the decryption (length, range, padding, hash, separator, wrong digest) is the one error E_COERCE with the message decryption error, so the error tells nothing about the padding. RAW returns the full modulus-length block with its leading zero bytes. The private operation uses the Chinese remainder theorem and is checked with the public exponent. Parameter order and message-format options were compared with the module source (RSA Verify message formats are Raw, Hex, Base64; Forge adds Latin-1 and reads Raw as UTF-8, and the result texts Verified OK and Verification Failure are CyberChef's).

Cross-checked in the wave 7 close-out against CyberChef 11.5.0 (module source read; the module was run on sample inputs for layouts). The SubjectPublicKeyInfo public key of every private key in the text, RSA or elliptic curve (RSA PRIVATE KEY, EC PRIVATE KEY, PRIVATE KEY with the RSA or id-ecPublicKey algorithm, encrypted forms with the password parameter; EC curves P-256, P-384, P-521, secp256k1), in order, as PUBLIC KEY PEM (CyberChef's only output), DER bytes or JWK (one line of JSON per key). The EC half is ecdsa:public-key, which stays a separate op. Differences: output has LF line ends (CyberChef writes CRLF); DSA keys, which CyberChef reads, are E_RANGE; no key block is E_RANGE where CyberChef returns nothing; the password and the DER and JWK formats are additions.
